description.narrative: This purpose of this project is to: 1) train and mentor a team of professionals for effective leadership in wildlife conservation; 2) establish a foundation for Chimpanzee conservation at Njala University; and 3) facilitate exchanges between conservation professionals in Sierra Leone and Liberia. The Chimpanzee is symbolic of the overall conservation dilemma in West Africa habitat fragmentation, bushmeat hunting, pet trade, and conflicts with humans that require innovative leaders for implementing effective and successful long-term solutions. Activities include: 1) Developing a team of wildlife conservation professionals by designing, organizing and implementing an 18-month MENTOR-CHIMP program on wildlife conservation and management through a combination of lectures, field work, team pilot projects and on-the-job training, and recruiting the team of eight working professionals (Fellows) from Sierra Leone and Liberia for dynamic mentoring by faculty members; 2) Establishing a Foundation for Chimpanzee Research and Monitoring at Njala University to facilitate long-term influence on research and academic training in Wildlife Conservation and Management; identifying long-term priorities for Chimpanzee conservation; mobilizing and engaging Njala University Staff; and establishing partnerships and institutional links; 3) Facilitating exchange visits between professionals in Sierra Leone and Liberia through engagement of Njala University faculty with counterparts at Cuttington University and the University of Liberia.
